sources.title: OpenAI Codex App Server architecture
sources.takeaway: Shared app-server harnesses support multiple Codex surfaces; THOS should keep app-lane orchestration status-only and watcher-backed.

sources.title: OpenAI Codex releases
sources.takeaway: Release surfaces are useful for drift awareness but installed-state checks remain the local truth source.

sources.title: OpenAI Codex plugin wrapper
sources.takeaway: Codex app-server delegation can share local authentication, config, checkout, and runtime state; THOS should avoid duplicate runtimes and prefer explicit local receipts.

sources.title: MCP security best practices
sources.takeaway: Consent, token audience, redirect/state validation, local-server consent, and confused-deputy resistance remain mandatory connector rules.

sources.title: Vertex AI Agent Engine Code Execution
sources.takeaway: Managed code-execution sandboxes, TTL, file limits, and stateful execution provide design patterns for THOS sandbox readiness receipts without implying cloud deployment.

sources.title: GKE Agent Sandbox
sources.takeaway: Strong process, storage, and network isolation via sandbox controllers reinforces THOS separation between advisory, watcher, and mutation lanes.

carry_forward_rules: Use background app-lane watchers for future x1 calls.
Do productive source/prep work while waiting.
Keep security and sandbox sources mapped to concrete THOS guardrails.
Keep all GMUT/THOS open gates intact.
